1_executive_summary: P-26 — Osmotic Pressure-Regulated Drainage Valve. A computationally specified P-26 concept plus a preregistered decisive experiment — not a validated technology. Current evidence: T1. Transfer posture: DECISIVE_EXPERIMENT_REQUIRED. Recommended transaction: SPONSORED_VALIDATION ($12K bench + fouling). Validation cost: $12K (includes 30-day soak).
2_industry_problem: NO_FAILURES_TESTED_YET — all evidence is MODELLED. Membrane fouling risk in CSF (protein, cells) not yet modeled. Long-term membrane integrity unknown.

3_current_alternative.strongest_alternative: Anti-siphon device (ASD) — established but binary. Osmotic valve offers proportional response without electronics.
3_current_alternative.alternative_weakness: ASD is mechanical (binary); osmotic is passive (proportional)

evidence_against: NO_FAILURES_TESTED_YET — all evidence is MODELLED. Membrane fouling risk in CSF (protein, cells) not yet modeled. Long-term membrane integrity unknown.
4_technology_advantage_hypothesis.unresolved_question: Does osmotic membrane maintain selectivity and permeability in CSF environment over 5+ year implantation? Membrane fouling is the primary risk.

5_evidence_level.evidence_ledger_summary: MODELLED: 3 claims, COMPUTATIONALLY_SUPPORTED: 0 claims, OBSERVED: 0 claims
5_evidence_level.honest_assessment: Computationally supported. No external validation yet. Evidence ledger is transparent and auditable.

6_remaining_uncertainty.primary_uncertainty: Does osmotic membrane maintain selectivity and permeability in CSF environment over 5+ year implantation? Membrane fouling is the primary risk.
known_failures: NO_FAILURES_TESTED_YET — all evidence is MODELLED. Membrane fouling risk in CSF (protein, cells) not yet modeled. Long-term membrane integrity unknown.
6_remaining_uncertainty.what_is_NOT_proven: No external validation. No physical prototype. No clinical data. No regulatory clearance. No manufacturing validation.

7_validation_investment.timeline: 10 weeks to T2, 12-18 months to T3
7_validation_investment.success_threshold: Advance to next development phase (see Development Plan)

8_strategic_buyer_fit.ideal_buyer: Shunt OEM seeking passive regulation technology (Miethke, Sophysa)
8_strategic_buyer_fit.buyer_type: Shunt OEM with membrane/material science capability
8_strategic_buyer_fit.strategic_reason: Osmotic regulation is a novel passive mechanism. No electronics, no moving parts. If membrane fouling is manageable, this is a highly reliable overdrainage prevention architecture.
8_strategic_buyer_fit.capabilities_required: Semi-permeable membrane manufacturing, CSF compatibility testing, long-term implant testing
8_strategic_buyer_fit.why_this_buyer_would_care: Passive, zero-maintenance overdrainage prevention. Membrane technology is a new approach to an old problem. The 30-day fouling test is the decisive question.

10_why_now: Passive, zero-maintenance overdrainage prevention. Osmotic regulation is a novel mechanism — no electronics, no moving parts. Membrane technology has matured. Fouling test is the decisive question. New candidate (R347).
